topic: sub:12|Trigonometry|Sine rule for an obtuse angle

figures.cap: triangle with sides 9.2 cm, 14 cm, angle 13°25' and obtuse angle x

parts.latex:
Calculate the size of the angle marked $x$, given that it is an obtuse angle. Give your answer correct to the nearest minute.

\exfigure{2839_q1c_1}

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule,
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{\sin x^\circ}{14} &= \dfrac{\sin 13^\circ 25'}{9.2} \\ \sin x^\circ &= \dfrac{14\sin 13^\circ 25'}{9.2} = 0.353\ldots \\ x^\circ &= 20.676\ldots^\circ \text{ or } 180^\circ-20.676\ldots^\circ = 159.32\ldots^\circ\end{aligned}$$
But $x^\circ$ is obtuse, so
$$x = 159^\circ 19' \text{ (to the nearest minute)}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Applies the sine rule to find $\sin x^\circ$, or equivalent merit

meta.marker_note: This question should have been out of 3. Deduct 1 mark if the obtuse angle is not given, but no penalty if rounded to the nearest degree.

figures.cap: triangle with angle 23°37', sides 54.1 cm and 25 cm, obtuse angle theta

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule,
$$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{54.1}=\dfrac{\sin 23^\circ37'}{25}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \theta &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{54.1\sin 23^\circ37'}{25}\right) \\ &= 60^\circ 6' \end{aligned}$$
Since $\theta$ is obtuse (ambiguous case),
$$\theta=180^\circ-60^\circ6'=119^\circ54'$$
criteria: Correct answer to the nearest minute
Uses the ambiguous case, or equivalent merit
Correct application of the sine rule, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: triangle ABC with AB=6 cm, AC=10 cm, angle C = 20°41'

solutions.latex:
Applying the sine rule in triangle $ABC$:
$$\dfrac{\sin \angle ABC}{10} = \dfrac{\sin 20^\circ 41'}{6}$$
$$\sin \angle ABC = \dfrac{10 \sin 20^\circ 41'}{6}$$
The calculator gives $36^\circ 4'$, but $\angle ABC$ is obtuse, so
$$\begin{aligned} \angle ABC &= 180^\circ - 36^\circ 4' \\ &= 143^\circ 56' \end{aligned}$$
Using the angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle BAC &= 180^\circ - 143^\circ 56' - 20^\circ 41' \\ &= 15^\circ 23' \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds $\sin \angle ABC$, or equivalent merit
Attempts to find an angle in the triangle, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: triangle with angle 23°37', sides 54.1 cm and 25 cm, obtuse angle theta

solutions.latex:
Let the angle $\theta$ be opposite the side of length $54.1$ cm, and the angle $23^\circ37'$ be opposite the side of length $25$ cm. Use the sine rule.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{\sin\theta}{54.1} &= \dfrac{\sin 23^\circ37'}{25} \\ \sin\theta &= \dfrac{54.1\sin 23^\circ37'}{25} \\ &\approx 0.8669 \end{aligned}$$
The calculator gives the acute angle $\sin^{-1}(0.8669)\approx 60^\circ6'$.

Since $\theta$ is obtuse,
$$\begin{aligned} \theta &= 180^\circ-60^\circ6' \\ &= 119^\circ54' \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \theta = 119^\circ54'$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds $\sin\theta$ and the acute angle, or equivalent merit
Writes the sine rule with the correct substitutions, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule in the triangle:
$$\dfrac{\sin 23^\circ 37'}{25} = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{54.1}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \sin\theta &= \dfrac{54.1 \times \sin 23^\circ 37'}{25} \\ &\approx 0.8669321037 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \theta &\approx 60^\circ 6' 14.63'' \\ &\approx 60^\circ 6' \end{aligned}$$
$\theta$ is obtuse, so
$$\theta = 180^\circ - 60^\circ 6' = 119^\circ 54'$$
$$\therefore\ \theta \approx 119^\circ 54'$$

parts.latex:
\exfigure{713_q10_1}

The diagram above shows a triangle with side lengths 25 cm, 47 cm and angles $30^\circ$ and $\theta$. What is the value of the obtuse angle $\theta$ to the nearest degree?

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule:

$$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{47}=\dfrac{\sin 30^\circ}{25}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \sin\theta &= \dfrac{47\sin 30^\circ}{25} \\ \theta &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{47\sin 30^\circ}{25}\right) \\ &= 70^\circ \end{aligned}$$

The obtuse angle is $180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ$, so option C is correct.
criteria: Correct answer

figures.cap: triangle with sides 12 m and 16 m, angle 47° and obtuse angle θ

parts.latex:
Find the size of the obtuse angle $\theta$ in the following triangle.

\exfigure{1246_q12_1}

solutions.latex:
By the sine rule,
$$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{16} = \dfrac{\sin 47^\circ}{12}$$
Hence
$$\theta = 77.197\ldots^\circ$$
The angle is obtuse, so
$$\begin{aligned} \theta &= 180^\circ - 77.197\ldots^\circ \\ &= 102.8^\circ \text{ (1 d.p.)} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \theta \approx 102.8^\circ$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the acute angle $77.197\ldots^\circ$, or equivalent merit
Correct use of the sine rule, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Given that $\sin\theta=\dfrac{5\times\sin 40^\circ}{6}$ and $\theta$ is obtuse, what is the size of $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree?

solutions.latex:
$$\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5\times\sin40^\circ}{6}\right)\approx32^\circ$$

Since $\theta$ is obtuse, $\theta=180^\circ-32^\circ=148^\circ$.

Hence the answer is option A.
